items.excerpt: A Spoken-commissioned survey found 61% of listeners mistook AI narration for human voices and the same share favored AI narration in multi-character scenes, even as a separate Audio Publishers Association study showed overall willingness to try AI-narrated audiobooks slipping year over year.

An Edison Research blind test found listeners rated AI multi-cast narration slightly better than single human narration for character-driven scenes, with 65% saying they'd try the full audiobook after hearing the AI version versus only 31% willing to try an AI-narrated title upfront.

Creative Access's 2026 'Thrive' report finds publishing has the lowest AI uptake of any creative industry at just 6%, reflecting ongoing concerns around copyright and authorship even as adjacent creative sectors adopt AI tools far faster.

Self-Publishing News (July 16, 2026): Dale L. Roberts breaks down the new survey data showing listeners increasingly accept AI multi-cast audiobook narration, and what the human-vs-AI narration split means for indie authors' production and budgeting decisions.

Robert Moor argues publishing faces a growing 'hologram problem': AI summarizers, chat tools, marketing blurbs and podcasts now convey a book's substance so convincingly that readers increasingly consume the simulacrum instead of reading the book itself, reshaping how titles are written, sold and read.
